title: Italian Game
intro: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4: fast development and a bishop aimed at f7. A classic first opening for White.

lessons.title: First moves and the Giuoco Piano
lessons.summary: Develop quickly, then build a big centre with c3 and d4.

steps.text: The Italian Game starts 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4. White develops fast and points the bishop at f7, the weakest square near Black's king.
Play the first moves of the Italian: e4, then Nf3, then Bc4.
steps.hint: King's pawn two squares, then the king's knight, then the bishop.
steps.ifWrong: That is playable, but the Italian goes e4, Nf3 and Bc4.

steps.text: The bishop on c4 eyes f7. Black's main answers are 3...Bc5, the Giuoco Piano ('quiet game'), and 3...Nf6, the Two Knights.
You want to play d4 next. Prepare it with c3, so you can take back on d4 with a pawn.
steps.hint: A pawn move that supports d4.
steps.ifWrong: Here the plan is c3, getting ready for d4.

feedback.d2d3: The quiet d3 is a fine modern choice too. This lesson shows the classic plan with c3 and d4.

steps.text: Black develops and attacks your e4 pawn with 4...Nf6.
Strike in the centre with d4.
steps.hint: The pawn on c3 supports it.
steps.ifRight: Pawns on e4 and d4: a big centre. Next you castle and bring out the rest.

lessons.title: The Two Knights and the attack on f7
lessons.summary: Ng5 hits f7 twice: know the attack and Black's defence.

steps.text: In the Two Knights, Black plays 3...Nf6 and attacks e4 instead of copying with ...Bc5.
Go for f7: put a second piece on it with the knight.
steps.hint: The knight can jump to a square that attacks f7.
steps.ifWrong: This lesson looks at the sharp Ng5, attacking f7 twice.
steps.ifRight: Knight and bishop both hit f7.

feedback.d2d3: The calm d3 is a good modern choice. Here, try the sharp Ng5.
feedback.e1g1: Castling is fine and solid. Here, try the sharp Ng5.

steps.text: Black's best defence is 4...d5, blocking the bishop. After 5.exd5 Black must not take back with the knight.
Here Black took back with 5...Nxd5. Now f7 is weak, and White can attack it with a piece or a pawn.
Black took back with 5...Nxd5. Find a strong attacking move.
steps.hint: Open the centre with a pawn, or sacrifice the knight on f7 (the Fried Liver Attack).
steps.ifWrong: Keep the pressure on f7 and the centre.
steps.ifRight: That keeps Black's king under fire.

feedback.d1f3: It hits f7 and d5, but it leaves your knight on g5 unprotected: ...Qxg5 wins it.
